conviction_note: The Q3 numbers are new, because nothing was pre-released and there is no profit warning on NewsWeb. abs_move is set at 6.0 from the 7% European base for unreleased numbers, trimmed for a qualitative-only outlook and a large-cap tape. p_up is 46 because the one directional lean (aftermarket still held back by a persisting Hormuz/energy shock, with Wärtsilä service sales down 2%) is a proxy that DNB Carnegie's 16 Oct sell call and the -4.2% 20-day tape have already partly priced. The finding sum (-0.6) and the scaled number (-0.48) agree in sign and size.

already_public.what: Q3 report date and time: 07:00 CET Friday 30 October 2026, webcast 08:15 CET

Outlook as of Q2: double-digit newbuild delivery growth in 2026; 0-5% growth short-to-medium term; MNOK 600 cost programme with full effect in 2027; CMD ambition of 10% revenue CAGR and EBITDA margin above 16% over time; aftermarket held back by customers delaying non-urgent service after the Strait of Hormuz closure
Berg Propulsion acquisition completed 1 Oct (it consolidates from Q4, not Q3); Steerprop acquisition agreed 7 Sep
Q3 contract announcements with undisclosed values: Cadeler WTIV integrated package (3 Sep) and Austal Kamewa waterjets for 18 landing craft (10 Sep); IWS four CSOVs on 13 Oct falls in Q4

new_in_release.expect: Q3 revenue up modestly y/y on newbuild deliveries. EBITDA likely below the Q3'25 comparable of MNOK 1,143 (18.1%) and below an unverified ~MNOK 1,200 consensus snippet; aftermarket flat-to-down. Lean slightly negative.

No numeric guide is given. The risk is the aftermarket wording: Q2 said positive H2 momentum was expected (Quartr summary), and a softening of that with Hormuz/energy still disrupted would be negative. Unknown, slight negative lean.
Order intake and book-to-bill: strong yard contracting (Clarksons 2,552 contracts vs 1,200) and Q3 wins argue for book-to-bill at or above 1. Mild positive.
unknown; M&A outflow for Berg falls in Q4, funded by the NOK 2.5bn August bond
Q3 may carry M&A transaction costs (Berg, Steerprop) and residual demerger costs, as Q2 carried MNOK 37 of demerger cost. Small negative one-off.

findings.finding: The aftermarket drag the company blamed on the Strait of Hormuz closure looks unresolved through Q3: Brent ~$100, TTF >€100/MWh and reduced Qatari deliveries are still being cited in late October, and peer Wärtsilä's Q3 service net sales fell 2% (EUR 802m vs 815m). That cuts against management's Q2 line that positive aftermarket momentum was expected in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (aftermarket softness, margin down y/y): -5.79%. Q2 2026 (EBITDA 830 vs 881 expected, aftermarket slower but up q/q): +0.82%.
findings.original_quote: E24 2026-10-29 on macro: 'Konkurranse om LNG: Økt asiatisk etterspørsel etter LNG og reduserte leveranser fra Qatar forsterker tilbudskvisen i Europa' (Competition for LNG: higher Asian demand and reduced deliveries from Qatar tighten supply in Europe); KMAR Q2: 'we have experienced customers delaying service that is not urgent. This has put a temporary break in aftermarket growth.'
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. DNB Carnegie cut to sell on 16 Oct and the stock is -4.2% over 20 days, but the 5-day tape is +1.1% and the consensus snippet (~16.9% margin) still looks rich against a Q2 12.5% margin. If the drag were fully priced, the Wärtsilä day (27 Oct, WRT -8.3%) would have carried KMAR down; KMAR was +0.57% that day and -2.98% the next.
findings.independence: Wärtsilä Q3 interim report, service net sales -2% (https://www.wartsila.com/gbr/media/news/27-10-2026-wartsila-s-interim-report-january-september-2026-3806530); E24 macro on gas/oil (https://e24.no/bors/nyheter?pinnedEntry=304695); DNB Carnegie sell 16 Oct (https://www.placera.se/telegram/kongsberg-maritime-dnb-carnegie-sanker-kongsberg-maritime-till-salj-behall-riktkurs-55-norska-kronor-50-20261016)

findings.finding: Newbuild demand stayed strong in Q3: Clarksons counted 2,552 newbuild contracts in the period against 1,200 a year earlier (per Wärtsilä), and KMAR announced Q3 wins including a complete electrical, automation and propulsion package for two Cadeler WTIVs and waterjets for 18 Australian Army landing craft. That supports order intake and book-to-bill at or above 1 and a further record backlog.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 record backlog (MNOK 28,406, B2B 1.09) came with a +0.82% day despite an EBITDA miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Contract values were undisclosed, so no estimate can be anchored on them. Analysts see the same yard data, though, so the size is small. If it were fully priced, the post-Barclays and Fearnley initiations rally (to 64 on 22 Sep) would have held; the stock has since given back about 8%.

findings.finding: The y/y comparison is hard: Q3 2025 EBITDA was MNOK 1,143 at an 18.1% margin, with Energy & Control at 16.8%, its best quarter in the series. A Q3 2026 margin near the H1 13.0% would print a headline EBITDA decline of 15-25% y/y.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 printed EBITDA 893 vs 2,121 (one-off-inflated comp) and fell 5.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in the company's own quarterly table, so estimates already carry it, hence near zero. It only matters if a y/y-decline headline drives selling at the open.

findings.finding: Q3 likely carries M&A transaction costs for Berg Propulsion (completed 1 Oct) and Steerprop (agreed 7 Sep), on top of the residual demerger costs that took MNOK 37 out of Q2. This is a small one-off below the run-rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 one-offs (FX 34, demerger 37) were looked through: +0.82% on an EBITDA miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Size unknown and probably flagged as non-recurring; the market looked through Q2's one-offs, so the size is a fraction.

findings.finding: Analyst flow into the print is split: Fearnley initiated at buy 72 (22 Sep), Barclays at overweight 74 (29 Sep), SB1 cut its target to 70 from 75 (30 Sep), Pareto put KMAR into its October portfolio (1/4 Oct), and DNB Carnegie cut to sell, target 55 (16 Oct).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: June DNB Carnegie sell call: -7% on the day (MarketMate).
findings.original_quote: DNB Carnegie sänker Kongsberg Maritime till sälj (behåll), riktkurs 55 norska kronor (50) (DNB Carnegie cuts Kongsberg Maritime to sell (from hold), target NOK 55 (50))
findings.why_not_priced: All of it is public broker flow and already in the tape (spot 59, between the 55 sell target and the 70-74 buy targets), so it is sized at zero. It is filed because it shows sentiment into the print is balanced rather than crowded.

baseline_tension: The small negative lean agrees with the -4.2% 20-day run-up and with DNB Carnegie's sell call, and slightly opposes the baseline's priced_lean of +0.21. Because it agrees with visible sell-side flow it is partly priced, which is why p_up sits at 46 rather than lower.
language_note: The NewsWeb flagging notices on Folketrygdfondet's share lending are Norwegian only ('Folketrygdfondet har i dag 24. september 2026, lånt ut 155 000 aksjer'). They are immaterial.

The Norwegian (E24) press carried the Q2 consensus miss (EBITDA 830 vs 881 expected), the Pareto October portfolio switch into KMAR, and the late-October gas and oil context. English sources carried none of these, but no Norwegian source carried a Q3 preview or consensus.
The broker-flow headlines (DNB Carnegie sell 16 Oct, SB1, Barclays, Fearnley) reached me through Swedish Finwire copy on placera.se and Nordnet, not through English wires.
The issuer's own filings are all in English, so on the filing side the Norwegian sources added nothing.
lessons_applied: 'Too small about the move' and the 7% base for unreleased numbers: abs_move_pct raised from 5.0 to 6.0. It stays below 7 because the outlook is qualitative-only and the name is a $6m/day large cap.
Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis: the aftermarket finding goes from -1.0 to -0.8 because part of it rests on oil and gas macro rather than a company or counterparty number.
A narrow proxy loses to a broad series: the newbuild finding goes from +0.6 to +0.5.
A finding about a number the market already has is worth about 0: the tough-comparison finding goes from -0.4 to -0.2 because the Q3'25 comparable is in the company's own table.
One-off sized at a fraction: M&A costs go from -0.2 to -0.1.
File every sourced fact: the split analyst-flow item is added as a 0.0 positioning finding.
